title: How sage is built, at two zoom levels

blocks.text: Zoom 1 shows what sage talks to. Zoom 2 shows the parts inside sage. Each picture has 6 boxes or fewer.

blocks.title: Sage, zoom 1 of 2: what it talks to
blocks.key: Key: [type] of each part. Double box: the system that this picture is about. Each arrow goes one way, and its label says what it does. Left out: the board page, which you open in a browser on your Mac (zoom 2 shows the board).
lines: │ Ask for work, answer questions, review     │
│ The desktop app or a terminal              │
║ A chief and a team of agents that design,  ║
║ build, review and prove each change        ║
│ Holds the code and runs the checks         │

blocks.title: Sage, zoom 2 of 2: the parts inside
blocks.key: Key: [type] of each part. Double box: the part that you talk to. Left out: the hooks that check each command; the designer and the engineer's check, which the chief starts before the lead; the lead's own records in the logbook.

blocks.label: What changes for you
blocks.text: Nothing. This is the map that later design questions start from.

blocks.label: What I need from you
blocks.text: Nothing. Tell me if a box or an arrow is wrong.
